findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates a single array on the class prototype, so every instance of CreateAccountController (and any re-opened modal) mutates and reads the same array. Emails rejected in one session will persist/leak into later ones, and the array never resets. It should be initialized per-instance (e.g. in `init`, `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`).

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` does an exact match. User emails are not guaranteed to be stored/submitted in the same case as the blocked record, so `Bad@Spam.com` bypasses a block entry for `bad@spam.com`. Downcase both on write (before_validation) and on lookup.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment and silent save failure
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads-modifies-writes outside a transaction, so concurrent signup attempts lose increments. Also `save` return value is ignored, so a validation/DB failure silently drops the statistic. Prefer `increment!`/`update_columns` with a SQL increment.

findings.title: should_block? side effect runs on every validation, inflating match_count
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates state (match_count/last_match_at). `validate_each` can be invoked multiple times per request (e.g. `user.valid?` in UsersController#create followed by `user.save`), so a single signup attempt can bump the counter several times, making the statistic unreliable.
